annotations.title: Cron checker: validate expressions and flag never-firing schedules

description: Validate 5-field cron expressions, name the field that is out of range, and flag the day-of-month and day-of-week combination that most implementations treat as 'either', so a schedule that never fires is caught. Choose this to validate 5-field cron expressions, to have an out-of-range field named, and to catch the day-of-month plus day-of-week combination that most implementations treat as 'either' and that makes a job never fire. Do not choose this when you need the next fire time or a timezone conversion; it validates field syntax only. Example requests: Check these cron expressions for mistakes. | Why does this cron job never run? Here are the expressions. | Validate my cron scheduled jobs before I deploy them.

accepted_price.description: The amount accepted, exactly as quoted (for example "5.00" or 5). Checked against the stored quote, so a price that moved between quote and authorize is refused rather than silently absorbed. Optional, but sent to make the acceptance explicit.

authorized_by.description: Identifier of the human or agent authorizing this job.

content.description: The customer's input.txt, as text. Supported: Plain text. Maximum 1048576 bytes.

inputs.title: Cron checker: validate expressions and flag never-firing schedules

quote_id.description: The quote_id returned by POST /v1/jobs. Required to authorize a priced capability; the service rejects a priced job that does not name the quote it issued.

name: submit_cron_expression_check

access_token.description: Per-job credential. Present it as the X-Job-Token header to read the job or list it. Keep it; it is the only credential for this job.

verification.description: Independent verification. verification.ok = false means the job failed, not a partial success.
